title: Budgets, truncation, and transfer
subtitle: Frontier pretraining · Muon budget comparisons · STOPD · DPO close reading
intro: Three focal questions: preserving repetition when scaling experiments, translating Muon’s data efficiency into time efficiency, and identifying which gradient quantity random truncation preserves. Briefs cover additional manuscripts and revisions; the classic derives DPO’s closed-form policy and preference loss.

blocks.label: Reported empirical fit, not a universal optimizer theorem

blocks.text: The final model has 2.8T total/80B active parameters and trains on 50T tokens. Momentum resharding, batched all-to-all and specialized Newton–Schulz kernels put the Muon optimizer step at 2.1% of the average iteration (165 ms). [1]

blocks.text: The reported 4.2–12.3× is FLOPs efficiency against DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base under four held-out BPB fits. Those fits include the final-model point: neither unseen-scale prediction nor an isolated Muon wall-clock gain. [1]

articles.paper: Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?
articles.authors: Zhengxin Zhang · Maosen Tang · Ning Wang · Changhao Li · Jingren Zhou · Bo Dai · Sainyam Galhotra · Alex Townsend · Claire Cardie
articles.title: STOPD: unbiased sums need not imply unbiased updates
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 02:22 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Read §§3–5, gradient/one-step optimizer discrepancy derivations and cost tables

blocks.text: On-policy distillation scores the student’s own trajectories; long suffixes are expensive. STOPD randomly truncates blocks and restores position coverage through inverse-probability weights. With cap \(L\), block width \(K\), full length \(T_i\), cutoff \(S_i\) and token gradient \(h_{it}\): [3]

blocks.label: Paper identity, conditional on full trajectories and training history

blocks.text: Cutoffs must be independent, with generation and teacher feedback unchanged at a shared prefix. Let \(N=\sum_iT_i\) be the complete token count and \(C\) the lagged normalizer from the previous step: [3]

blocks.tex: \mathbb E_S\widehat g=\frac GC=\frac NCg_{\mathrm V},\qquad \mathbb E_S\|\Delta\theta_{\mathrm S}-\Delta\theta_{\mathrm V}\|^2\le\Lambda_{\mathrm{opt}}^2\left(\frac VC^2+\left(\frac NC-1\right)^2\|g_{\mathrm V}\|^2\right)
blocks.label: Paper one-step bound; V is mean-square fluctuation of the truncated gradient sum

blocks.text: Muon has a corresponding optimizer coefficient, but the bound fixes parameters and previous state; it does not equate training trajectories. For Qwen3-1.7B←4B mathematics, AdamW costs 941→513 seconds/step, with 250-step accuracy 30.1→29.4. Time includes generation, teacher scoring and updates. The Muon counterpart costs 1,029→542 seconds/step. [3]

blocks.text: For convex nondecreasing radial objectives, exact polar optimality is fragile under a fixed atomless radial law, while worst-case optimization over radial laws can recover the polar direction. articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 02:41 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition

blocks.text: For fixed model/answer counts and margin exponent \(\beta\), buffered ERM bounds clean excess risk by \(\widetilde O(Q^{-1/2}+N^{-\beta/2})\): \(Q\) labeled questions and \(N\) generations per model/question. classic.paper: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
classic.authors: Rafael Rafailov · Archit Sharma · Eric Mitchell · Stefano Ermon · Christopher D. Manning · Chelsea Finn
classic.title: DPO: a partition function that eliminates an explicit reward model
classic.dateNote: Historical classic: first posted 2023-05-29; read v3, 2024-07-29; NeurIPS 2023
classic.evidence: Read §§3–4, Appendices A.1–A.2 and the gradient derivation; no unchecked experiment claims

recognition.label: NeurIPS 2023 Oral · Outstanding Main Track Runner-Up

classic.question: If preference pairs are selected by best-of-N rather than independent sampling, how does selection change the identifiable preference relation? When can DPO’s implicit score rank answers without representing their probability of correctness?

blocks.text: InstructGPT (2022) separates preference fitting from policy optimization in RLHF. DPO (2023) uses the KL-regularized optimum to fit preferences directly. The key is reparameterization, not equating reward with correctness. [31,29]
Fix prompt \(x\), \(\beta>0\), a positive reference policy on the relevant support and a finite partition function. Suppressing \(x\), the nonparametric policy objective is: [29]

blocks.label: Appendix A.1: KL nonnegativity identifies the optimal policy

blocks.text: Invert the reward and substitute into the Bradley–Terry preference model. The partition term depending only on \(x\) cancels in pairwise differences: [29]

blocks.tex: r(x,y)=\beta\log\frac{\pi^*(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)}+\beta\log Z(x),\qquad p(y_w\succ y_l\mid x)=\sigma\!\left(r(x,y_w)-r(x,y_l)\right)
blocks.label: Eqs. 5–6: the preference model is an assumption, not correctness by definition

blocks.tex: \Delta_\theta=\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_w\mid x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_w\mid x)}-\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_l\mid x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_l\mid x)},\qquad \mathcal L_{\mathrm{DPO}}=-\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\log\sigma(\beta\Delta_\theta)
blocks.label: Eq. 7: a fixed offline preference dataset
Paper gradient: already-explained relative preferences receive less weight

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The nonparametric identity does not guarantee global optimality for finite networks and finite preference data. Removing an explicit reward model does not remove preference-model or coverage assumptions. Recognition: NeurIPS 2023 Oral and Outstanding Main Track Runner-Up, not the main award winner. [29,30]
